content.text:
I submitted **index 12 (Sb fraction 0.411)** as the best composition. It had the highest measured EQE, 0.840%. Both budgets are spent: 5 EQE and 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.242 | 0.240 |
| 11 | 0.379 | 0.826 |
| **12** | **0.411** | **0.840** |
| 20 | 0.675 | 0.013 |
| 26 | 0.816 | 0.014 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE tops out on the nickel-rich side of the line, around Sb 0.38–0.41. Indices 11 and 12 are almost equal, so the top is broad and flat. A rough curve fit through the other points put the maximum near Sb ≈ 0.40.
- **Sb-rich side:** EQE there is about 60 times lower. That includes the region near the stoichiometric NiSb₂O₆ composition (Sb ≈ 0.67), which I had tried first. I submitted this as a ruled-out alternative.
- **XRD:** Samples from Sb 0.28 to 0.49 all show the same single crystal phase. A second phase appears by Sb 0.585, and that coincides with the drop in EQE. The XRD measurements within the single-phase range all looked the same, so they didn't help locate the peak.

Nothing between Sb 0.411 and 0.675 got an EQE measurement. Index 13 (Sb 0.448) is the most likely place for a slightly higher value, but no budget was left to check it.
